w: On 2 June 1970, in London, Davies, a reporter from a news agency, came to meet Yogiji Maharaj. He held a spiritual question and answer session with Swamishri. Some extracts from it:
Davies: "Not looking at women, not talking with them, not eating meat: all these rules are very hard to follow in this country and in Africa. What do you say about that?"
Swamishri: "Our God, Sahajanand Swami, has given strict rules. With His blessings all the rules can be followed..."
Davies: "What influence do you have on ordinary people? How are you the inner knower of all souls?"
Swamishri: "Shriji Maharaj gave such divine power to Bhagatji Maharaj and to our guru, Shastriji Maharaj. After that He gave the power to please all people and to give spiritual discourses."
Swamishri answered in this spirit: "My guru was the inner knower. I am only his servant."

In the evening assembly, the drama 'Charan Kamalna Ful' was performed. The drama described the courageous stories of children-devotees who had remained steadfast in their morals and faith amidst opposition and enticements. Finally Swamishri, in his blessings, underscored the virtues of faith, devotion and morality with reference to stories of children in the drama. 6,000 devotees availed of the special Children's Day program.

Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Radha Krishna Dev and Guru Parampara at the newly built Swaminarayan Mandir. The Governor Shri Dineshnandan Sahay and Mayor Shri Tarun Chatterjee and other dignitaries attended the function.

In the evening assembly Viveksagar Swami concluded his 11-day exposition on the Harililakalpataru. Finally Swamishri blessed the assembly, “The father believes that his son has grown up, but in fact his life has been shortened. Whatever that is to be done is possible during the years of youthhood. In old age the eyes lose their sight and one cannot do darshan, the hand cannot tell the mala, the body becomes weak and one cannot do what one desires to do so. If you wait to do things later in old age then your life becomes worthless85” In his book on the Bhagvad Gita, former General of the Indian Army, Lt. Gen. Dr S.B.S. Kochar, writes his experience of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and of his visits to Akshardham in Gandhinagar:

My Inspiration My initiation to spirituality was characterized by meeting and interacting with Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj at Akshardham in Gandhinagar sometime in 1992. His darshan filled me with such calm, assurance and ease that a quiet aroma of spirituality did not abandon me for weeks. It was much later that I came to know that Pramukh Swami Maharaj was the fifth spiritual successor of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the leader of a world-acclaimed socio-spiritual organisation, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha. To me, however, it was his simplicity and gentle humility that penetrated the core of my soul. He lives an ordinary life with an extraordinary goal – to spread the message of love and compassion. Whenever I went to Akshardham I felt at peace, totally at peace. The golden murti of Bhagwan Swaminarayan had so much spiritual aura and I experienced unbroken joy and harmony. I found Akshardham a fountain of spirituality, ‘universal’ in outlook, composition, expression and teachings. I felt rejuvenated, re-energised, refurbished – a different person. That was my first step to spiritual living. I was happy to renounce ‘food of violence’ and alcohol. Swamiji opens the locked door and takes us beyond our mundane existence to a life of joy and bliss. He provides pragmatic solutions to everyday living.
Lt. Gen. (Dr.) S.B.S. Kochar

Swamishri was doing his morning puja inside the mandir hall. Outside, the rains were pouring heavily and the winds were blowing at gale force. Normally Swamishri does darshan of Thakorji before doing his puja. But today, due to the stormy weather, Swamishri became engaged in doing his puja first. Midway through his puja someone suggested to Swamishri that he go for Thakorji’s darshan in the evening because of the inclement weather. Swamishri firmly replied, “Never say no for Thakorji’s darshan. No matter how heavy the rains are or how cold it may be, but never say no for Thakorji’s darshan. Then someone made another suggestion, “Swamishri if you are driven by car to the sea shore and the car is parked before the mandir podium then you will be able to have darshan of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj.” But Swamishri explicitly rejected the proposal, “Do not ever think in this manner. I want to go for Thakorji’s darshan.” By the time Swamishri completed his puja the rains had stopped completely. Swamishri’s resolve to go for darshan reveals his deep faith and devotion to Bhagwan Swaminarayan and his gurus.

Every day Pramukh Swami Maharaj had been remembering the devotees of the village of Pandari. Today these devotees came for darshan during the meetings. In particular, the sons of Ambarambhai, the son of Devji Bhagat of this village, came for darshan. Swamishri lovingly met them and praised their seva.

Today, when Mahant Swami Maharaj came to the steps of the Yagnapurush Smruti Mandir, on the occasion of the inauguration of the new batch of the "BAPS Swaminarayan Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya," he sanctified the new students' books by placing flowers on them. Then, right away, he himself began removing the flowers placed on the books. Everyone watched this action of Swamishri in wonder. Later everyone realised that the flowers had fallen on the faces of Shriji Maharaj and the gurus, so Swamishri had moved them away. What subtle devotion!

After darshan at the Yagnapurush Smruti Mandir, Mahant Swami Maharaj was sitting in a golf cart moving towards the assembly hall when the attendant sadhu began to present a devotee's question. But Swamishri's eyes and mind were on the devotees standing on either side, having darshan and praying. After pausing for a few moments, the attendant sadhu raised the matter again. Swamishri did not take his attention away from the devotees. The attendant sadhu waited a little again, then raised the matter a third time. Swamishri, a little irritated, said, "Later..."

Swamishri's wish is always to give every devotee as much benefit as possible. He does not like anyone to be left out because he is busy talking. The attendant sadhu understood, but joked, "If it were Pramukh Swami Maharaj, he would do two things at once!"
Swamishri's devotion to his guru welled up, and he said, "He would do four... our feet cannot fit in his stirrups."
A spiritual seeker asked Mahant Swami Maharaj today, "What is my inclination (anga)?"
"That will come gradually as you struggle with it; you will know in time," said Swamishri.
The seeker asked further, "How should I become attached to you?"
"Keep up the interaction (keep up the association)," Swamishri answered.
"How should I interact? It is not possible to meet you every time, and if I write letters, that takes up a lot of your time too."
"Do it in your mind."
"If we do it in our minds, how will you answer?"
"Start, and the answer will come from within."
"But from within, won't the mind just say what it likes? You yourself will make us understand, won't you?"
"Yes, we ourselves."
The seeker asked further, "In the katha you spoke of the highest awareness, of believing him to be the complete doer, and of deep thought about the attainment. How should we do that?"
With feeling, Swamishri began to say:

"The attainment is very great. Purush means Akshar mukta. He creates countless universes. Countless such muktas fit into one part of Akshar, and Purushottam is infinitely beyond even that Akshar. That Aksharbrahman we have received in the form of the guru...

The guru should not have to ask, 'Did you do this? Did you do that?' You should tell him yourself. Do not keep deceit. He knows everything, inside and out. If the feeling is genuine, he will answer even through a blade of green grass, even through a small child. One has to look with alert eyes; then one will know."
The seeker asked, "You whom we have met, who are you?"
"The great sadhu. Shriji Maharaj, Gunatitanand Swami and the great sadhu: this is our straightforward understanding," said Swamishri.
